recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. No broader core follow-up is needed unless Pharmacy reopens Medication v2 mappings; keep FHIR-7816 separate because it concerns prescription validity rather than medication instance expiration.
issue_request: FHIR-7810 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request from the 2015 May DSTU QA process. It asked to populate the Medication batch/expirationDate v2 mapping with RXA-16 Substance Expiration Date and RXG-20 Substance Expiration Date, and a Jira comment concurred that RXD-19 Substance Expiration Date should also be added.
initial_application: SVN-migrated commit 651364cb098a623c36afc1d6b9d56578507d897c listed tracker #7810 and added RXA-16/RXG-20 to Medication.product.batch.expirationDate during medication v2 mapping cleanup, but it did not include the Jira comment's RXD-19 addition. The current source lineage is Medication.instance.expirationDate.
additional_context: Medication is active in source/fhir.ini, and fhir.ini records old Medication.batch.expirationDate mapping to current Medication.instance.expirationDate. Related FHIR-7816 was already audited on the combined branch and concerns removing RXD-19 from MedicationPrescription/MedicationRequest validityPeriod, a separate prescription-validity concept that does not conflict with this product-expiration mapping.
reconciliation: Updated source/medication/structuredefinition-Medication.xml so Medication.instance.expirationDate maps to RXA-16, RXG-20, and RXD-19 Substance Expiration Date.
source_changes: source/medication/structuredefinition-Medication.xml: added RXD-19 Substance Expiration Date to the v2 mapping for Medication.instance.expirationDate.

related_jiras.note: Same 2015 medication v2 mapping cleanup family and RXD-19 term, but it removed RXD-19 from MedicationPrescription/MedicationRequest validityPeriod and does not reverse the Medication product expiration mapping.
